steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I recall this place being industrial land, not suitable for a casual visit.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: This spot is the closest we have to Old Siesta, so just let me sit here quietly.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Is that so? Can you even see anything from here, when we're so far from there?

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: Rhodes Island's office should be pretty close to city hall. It's been two months since you've returned, and you haven't paid me a single visit.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Shouldn't the Mayor be swamped with work this time of year? How would you have time for family?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: When you're free, you should go stroll around the streets, listen to the people grumbling about you. Then you'll understand how you've been doing.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: There are many things that I could have done a better job with.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: As a Siestan, I want to ask the Mayor a question:

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Why have all the volcanoes, coasts, culture, and music that we're so proud of completely vanished? Why are there so many people struggling to integrate into their new lives, why doesn't city hall do anything to help them?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I want to pin the blame on city hall too, they should have prepared for the move sooner.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But as Herman Doykos's daughter, I still have to say this—it's been hard for you, Dad.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: When I came back this time, I had planned to help Rhodes Island establish a branch office here, but I understand the Infected in Siesta are facing some extra challenges right now.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: Columbia's pedantic word game with their laws is just another card for them to play.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: They don't care about the lives of these few Infected. They only want a slice of Siesta's future large-scale international trade pie.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: 8,573. I looked at the info. That is the number of registered Infected who settled in Siesta last month.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You can either impose a ban to prevent any more Infected from settling on Siesta's nomadic plates, or hand them a larger sum of money for their health insurance. From a bystander's point of view, the latter is not an option for city hall.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: There is no way I could have forgotten that my other daughter is Infected herself.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: In our short decades of history, Siesta has faced many difficulties, but the path Siesta takes is always in the hands of us Siestans.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: I will think of something... there is always a way.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Then allow me help you out a little.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: To square-off against Columbia's word games, you can likewise designate an area outside the nomadic city, and declare it for development, which will be done by the Infected.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: And as for what kind of work—my two friends, recently arrived, are also interested in helping. A budding logistics company should manage to provide many jobs.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: In addition, I will use Rhodes Island's resources to establish a treatment center for the Infected. This is something I've always wanted to do.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: For Schwarz's sake, and for many more innocents besides. I'm not just someone who needs your care, I'll find my own way to protect Siesta too.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: I seem to remember my daughter not having a degree in politics?

spans.text: I seem to remember my daughter

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I guess I've been unwillingly influenced, that's all.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: Politics is no simple thing, but I'm happy to hear that you have such thoughts.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: I'll earnestly consider the Infected treatment center you mentioned. And I'll continue cooperating with MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Ever since you became mayor, Siesta has been relatively relaxed towards the Infected.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Some people say you're just putting on a show to win the miners' support; others say you're just trying to make more money from tourism.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: And now, I'm more inclined to believe that the things you've been doing are related to Mom.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: You... When did you find out...?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Just earlier. I heard a little story about her.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You've never taken the initiative to tell me those stories, and rarely ever actively bring up Mom with me.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: Barbara was a Victorian. To the Siestans of the time, Victoria, who wanted to annex us, was our greatest enemy.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: I was busy with Columbian and Victoria diplomacy, but I never dared to let anyone know that my wife just happened to be from Victoria.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: But Barbara never took it to heart, she had her own things to do.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: She said she was protecting the city in her own way, and you too.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: 'Protecting the city in her own way...'

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: You never lived a day of your life with her, but what you said just now is exactly the sort of thing she'd say.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: She was a great woman.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: And she had a great daughter.

steps.name: Herman
steps.text: Thank you, Ceylon.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Uh, could you lower the camera a little, angle it upwards a bit, so I look a little more imposing... wait, too low. Alright, that's good.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Check the recorder too. Everything I say has to be crystal clear.
Hello, Mr. Adams Schwire. As always, I first wish you good health.
By the time this disc reaches you, I should have completed both my Siesta trip, and all the business objectives I sought to accomplish.
Perhaps you may still take this as a child's folly—no, your insight must have recognized the value of this city, the value of a free and independent entrepot.
I've known from my first day here in Siesta that I've been tailed by some of our people watching my every move, perhaps at your behest, or perhaps at that of your other heirs trying to obstruct me.
But that no longer matters. I've long since realized that trying to read your mind is a laborious and pointless endeavor.
But if you are the one standing opposite me, then I've won this time.

spans.text: the one standing opposite me, then I've won this time.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: What did you call me here for, exactly?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: To give you a report on the project. Mountaincomm Trade has signed an agreement with Siesta. If everything goes smoothly, construction will begin around autumn.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: When the logistics center's construction is complete, we'll open trade with three countries: Sargon, Victoria, and Columbia. As the supply chain matures, we'll increase our scope.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: The natural trading advantages that comes with the independent state of New Siesta and the locals' eagerness for foreign goods will give us confidence in any future developments here at Mountaincomm Trade.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: You've always told me about the future you envision and want to realize in MountainDash Logistics, and now we've taken the actual first step.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: I've already seen the report on this project. Well done. You didn't let me down. No, I should say that your growth makes me proud.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Give yourself a proper vacation for the rest of the summer.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Thank you for your approval, but there's another report you haven't seen yet.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: It's regarding the progress of 'Mountaincomm Trade' splitting from 'MountainDash Logistics'.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: From now on, 'Mountaincomm Trade' will cease to be a subsidiary of 'MountainDash Logistics', and the series of projects we'll do for New Siesta's core development will have no connection to MountainDash Logistics.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Do you understand what you're implying?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: As President and CEO of MountainDash Logistics, you will no longer have any right to interfere in Mountaincomm Trade's affairs. MountainDash Logistics will need not bear any of Mountaincomm Trade's liabilities or responsibilities.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Of course, making such a decision without you in the loop has its uncertainties in the process.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If you don't agree with my decision and follow up with legal action, I'm afraid I'll be in a lot of trouble.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: What I want to know is, why do it this way?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Isn't this a step you've always wanted to take?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Not having to care about the constraints of the Federation of Enterprises, letting MountainDash Logistics make an actual change across the land?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: You really have surprised me... It seems like you've mustered the strength to do this.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Of course. I found a reliable business partner.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The last few days of this Siestan holiday have shown me what a young, and yet vibrant city it is. Its youth carry with it plenty of problems though.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But it is precisely because of its youth that it holds unlimited possibilities.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: In fact, there's a question I've been thinking about for a long while. Just how is it that you, an old man on his way out, are able to keep an iron grip on the many faces in the family with their own clandestine agendas?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I thought and thought before I finally came to a conclusion: you've allowed yourself to become a symbol.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No one knows your true intentions, nor do they know whom amongst them has your confidence. This fear of the unknown leaves them with only one option: to acquiesce to you.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This is how you've manipulated the Federation of Enterprises and even Lungmen's economic lifelines for so many decades. I may not ever manage to learn this trick of yours, but... Such a style of control always meets an end.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: How will the Federation of Enterprises cope without their leader when you're gone? How many of them will take advantage of the chaos to recklessly reap personal profit? I think that's something you wouldn't want to happen either.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Perhaps you still have faith in your personal physician, but as the soon-to-be Commissioner of the Lungmen Guard Department, and also as part of the younger generation, I must make plans for a Lungmen future without you.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The Lungmen order can't rest in the hands of just one person.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: If I hadn't become a Messenger, I wouldn't have known about the various differences between the many countries and regions on this great land.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: The vast distances in between make communication difficult and cause the different cultures to grow into their own distinct styles.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: So when someone builds a bridge between these countries and regions, it's bound to trigger drastic change.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Many people instinctively fear this sort of change. Some prefer to stay passively conservative, and others look to take advantage of the turmoil for personal gain. But the act of changing the landscape itself surely has a positive significance to it.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: This is MountainDash's ambition, and also my own as a Messenger.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I've never regretted becoming an L.G.D. superintendent. But in this past few years, I've realized that I can do more than just maintain Lungmen's security. I also have the power to help build it.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The cooperation with Mountaincomm Trade is my bargaining chip. I believe international trade will be an indispensable part of Lungmen's future economic market.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And at that moment when they're all staring emptily at the legacy you've left behind, I will use my own means to secure a seat in Lungmen's Chamber of Commerce, and lead a new order.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No matter how brilliant a sunset is, a new sun will always rise.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Got all that, Snowsant?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Miss Swire, that whole speech...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Send this recording to Lungmen. I wish I could see the old man fuming with my own eyes, but I can probably imagine what it would look like.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I wouldn't be surprised if all my cards were frozen after a while.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: R-Really? Then, will we be stuck here...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Won't you lend me some money?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: If you really need my help, Miss Swire...!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Just kidding. I brought enough cash for the both of us to fully enjoy our vacation. Any further annoyances will have to wait until we return to Lungmen.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Alright, now that we're all done here for real, let's officially begin our holiday!

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: You should just give up on straightening that parasol. The sky started turning dark by the time you got it up, there's no more sun to block anymore.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: We gotta get the grill we used in our old shop up and running. It's almost been a year since we've set up a booth, but it's definitely going to be popular today!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Sandworm legs? But no one supplies that nowadays.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I found a seller at the fair earlier. I kept some for you, in the fridge behind the guitar!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Really? —Awesome!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Phew—Mr. Tom, I've got your cold drinks here! Anything else I can help you with?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Thank you so much, sweetheart. You've been so busy helping me with so many things. Here, this cone is for you!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Thank you~

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Are you guys going to sell barbecue again?

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: It's for a party tonight.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: A party? Why haven't I heard of it?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Let's all meet up before everyone from the shopping district moves! We won't know when we'll see each other next, or when we'll open another shop.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Be careful with the fire, everyone! And stay safe! Don't go too close to the beach at night!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'll do my best with anything else that needs doing!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Didn't you come here for a vacation with Swire?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ah, after spending a few days here, I think it's more fun this way!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hello... May I know how much this harmonica costs?

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: You can have it, if you like. But if you want an instruction book or something, then I'll take some of your money. Haha, that's how I make sure the people who buy instruments learn to play them!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Do you know how to play the harmonica, sir? What's it like?

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Course I do! The feeling of playing the harmonica, huh...?

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: It feels like the wind. When it blows through the leaves and they make that rustling sound, it feels like stepping on a beach with the seawater slapping the sand around. That's what it feels like.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: You'll know it too when the smoke from my grill rises and the strings on my guitar move.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Come, eat anything you want. Feel free to bring your own meat too, I can help you grill it!

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Hold on, I have some leftover streamers from the time I moved out, just wait a sec while I bring them here!

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: Wait, I'll come too!

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Enis, help me bring these over to the party.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Woah. Aren't these wine bottles from your collection? Feeling generous today?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Just treat it as a goodbye to the shopping district, and Old Siesta too.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: When I was a kid, the adults used to say that the volcano would erupt one day. And now, we're really leaving this beach and moving to a new home in the nomadic city.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: All homes end up demolished someday. Even this magnificent, sturdy nomadic city has no way to 'live' longer than that volcano.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Now that the volcano's waking up, Siesta can't sleep in anymore, we should just move along with the nomadic city.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: That's pretty transparent of you. So are you still sad to leave the shop...?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: What difference does it make? Even if I know there's no choice, I still have to prepare my goodbyes.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I think about that a lot, and still can't figure it out... I don't know where's the most meaningful place to be.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: If I go, then does that mean...?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: When I was your age, I wasn't thinking so much about such things.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: My head was full of places I wanted to run off to, I wanted to get to know all kinds of people, play all kinds of rock music, learn local languages and figure out how to fit them into a song.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: You know yourself, it was those days that I met Chuck in Siesta.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: We wanted to see the beautiful 'White Volcano' people kept talking about, but we spent months wandering the beach and volcanoes with no luck.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: And just as we were about to leave Siesta to continue chasing the legend, we found in a corner of the Fashion Street, a baby sleeping soundly.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: So we stayed in Siesta, opened a bar, Chuck continued his travels while I decided to hang back and see what this kid would grow up into. And here we are.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: If we hadn't found you, the 'White Volcano' would have been just a name on a legend.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Later, we adopted Lut, and then Liv... you've all been growing up, and you've also stopped laughing as much as you used to.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: But on that day of the trade fair, all the surfboards from the shop disappeared, and the three of you looked so flustered, drenched in hot spring water, but you looked so, so happy. Tell you the truth, I was happy too.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: In that moment, I was thinking it'd be nice if some of these changes let our family stay as happy we've ever been.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: After all, I care more about you kids than the White Volcano.

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: I also want to wait until the White Volcano's done renovating, then I'll...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Leave it for now. Our old friends can't wait any longer, so go bring the booze over, Enis.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: It's fine, kiddo. No need to worry about me.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Whether you want to stay here, or go see what's beyond Siesta—whatever your plans, just go for it, like I did when I was your age.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: If you wait till the strings are loose, you won't get to play the songs you want to sing!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Enis...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Eyjafjalla, why aren't you joining them?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm not good at dancing... and it's still a bit difficult for me to keep up with the rhythm...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Hmm... Well, then I'll keep you company for a bit. We can chat.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: The last time you came to see me, you said you were experiencing hallucinations and seeing sheep. I thought the hallucinations were some kind symptom of Oripathy, but back then... I saw it too.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: It was small and warm, leaning on my chest, listening to my heartbeat... I'm sure I saw it, and even felt it too.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: It's so strange... I don't know why, but it makes me suddenly think about my mom... even though I've never met her.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Eyjafjalla, just what was the sheep from that day...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...I had a dream where I was wearing Mutti's protective gear, played with two little sheep for a whole night, and they spoke to me a lot.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: That dream felt so familiar... it was just like when I was a little girl, together with my parents...
Some fireworks suddenly explode a little distance away. The sky is not yet dark, and the smoke leaves a long trail.
The children who sneakily set off the fireworks run away laughing, followed by their parents, laughing as they scold their children.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: When I was little, I didn't have much chance to play like that with my parents.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They spent all their time on volcanoes, so I fell in love with volcanoes too. But since that day I've been thinking, they're still climbing, even now, aren't they?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Perhaps my mother is still doing what she liked to do...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: But Eyjafjalla, isn't it strange for me to be thinking like this...?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: I keep thinking these last few days, it would be great if I could see that sheep again. Or if I could dream about it, like you were talking about.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Have you... seen that sheep again since?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: No, it was the last one I saw...

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey—Ladies! Enough sitting over there, come on over and have some barbecue!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Her barbecue is really tasty! Eyjafjalla, did you try it the last time you were here?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I don't remember... The last time I visited, Ceylon was still all huffy and puffy.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Hey, that's ancient history! Let's not bring it up.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Eyjafjalla, what are your thoughts on Siesta on this trip?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Compared to last time, it's... much more relaxed, and more romantic too.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You should visit more often, as long as your health permits.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: You'll be able to see it then, a better and better Siesta, thanks to the joint efforts of so many.
The two of them stand on the barrens, looking toward the sea. They can vaguely make out the shadows of some volcanoes.

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: When do you think they'll erupt?

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: When it happens, there'll be so much more work to do.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Yes. And when that time comes, we'll do a great job ourselves.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Or maybe, we'll get to see the little sheep again?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hello, Professor Keller...?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...Alright, I'll heading back now!

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: There's a little problem with the volcano observation data...

steps.name: Ceylon
steps.text: Is it going to erupt sooner?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: The data fluctuates a lot, so maybe it's just an anomaly, but...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: If there's really a problem, we'll make a broadcast. I'll be counting on you if it comes to that, Ceylon.
